A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAB benchmark and CMP framework. The main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original PAB and UCC retrieval experiments, component and training-data ablations, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds multi-weather evaluations and results for additional competing methods in Section 5.

M1.justification: The pose-aware encoder, identity-based hard negative mining, cross encoder, three training losses and inference reranking remain unchanged. Condensed equations and wording do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds substantial environmental test coverage through a PAB multi-weather evaluation: normal conditions plus wind, rain, snow, rain with snow, darkness, darkness with wind/rain/snow, and over-exposure (Table 2). The original PAB training/test data and UCC evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The PAB comparison adds MRA, WoRA and CAMeL in both zero-shot and 0.1M-training settings (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 3), substantially broadening the competing retrieval methods evaluated. Existing comparators remain, and UCC comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new weather protocol evaluates four component configurations using R@1 and mAP, including means across environmental conditions. Existing splits, training budgets, model settings and retrieval metrics are retained; precise construction settings for the environmental conditions are not documented.

E4.justification: New Table 2 systematically tests the robustness of the baseline, PE-only, IHNM-only and full CMP configurations across environmental conditions. This substantially extends the existing clean-condition component ablation, data-scale analysis and UCC distribution-shift evaluation, which remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new weather-table means aggregate conditions rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial weather results and six PAB comparator rows. New Table 2 reports mean R@1 of 67.12 for CMP versus 64.11 for the baseline; these are newly evaluated conditions. Retained PAB/UCC scores and Figure 5 values match v2. Appendix Table 6 in v2, renumbered Table 7 in v3, changes PAB's reported average word count from 52.0 to 50.3.

T1.justification: The attention, feature aggregation, contrastive, matching and masked-language loss mathematics are equivalent. Several displayed equations become inline and equation numbers change, without new definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same task, benchmark, method contributions and headline performance claims. The conclusion extends the effectiveness claim to multi-weather settings.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets environmental testing as evidence of CMP robustness relevant to round-the-clock smart-city use. Existing interpretations of pose information, negative mining, behavioral discrimination and OOD transfer, together with caption-quality qualifications, remain.

D1.justification: Dataset-generation instructions and the training, augmentation, hardware, runtime and top-128 reranking details remain the same in the main text and appendices. The existing dataset/model/code access statement moves to a footnote; the weather addition supplies no detailed implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for MRA, WoRA, CAMeL, MuSe-Net and additional image-text matching, person re-identification and anomaly research. Citation coverage expands, while the related-work taxonomy and the paper's novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses passages in dataset construction, experimental discussion and the conclusion, corrects '1,6000' anomaly types to '1,600', updates corresponding-author notation and adds acknowledgments. Section order and almost all appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a full-width weather table, expands and rearranges the comparison tables, and redraws Figure 5 more compactly with unchanged values. Several equations become inline. Other figures and appendix displays are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The additional competing methods and weather tests with component ablations broaden empirical validation beyond v2's existing PAB/UCC experiments. They provide useful evidence about environmental robustness while preserving the original results and implementation documentation. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of environmental-condition construction and the continued absence of uncertainty estimates.
